databaseInfo.purpose: Reference documentation for building an original component-based dieline generator. All geometry, parameter lists, part behaviors, assembly logic, and folding sequences are described from industry-standard packaging engineering knowledge and direct inspection of CefBox template parameter interfaces. No proprietary SVG/DXF/PDF file content is copied.
databaseInfo.importantDisclaimer: This file documents common packaging structures and part relationships derived from publicly visible parameter names, descriptions, and structural logic. It must not be confused with copying exact proprietary SVG/DXF/PDF geometry. All numeric defaults are educational estimates derived from standard carton engineering ratios and must be verified against physical prototypes before production use.
databaseInfo.coordinateConvention: origin at top-left of flat dieline layout. X increases rightward, Y increases downward.
databaseInfo.panelOrderConvention: Panels are numbered left-to-right in flat layout: 1=glue-tab, 2=back, 3=side-A, 4=front, 5=side-B
databaseInfo.foldDirectionConvention: Valley fold = fold toward viewer (mountain on printed side). Mountain fold = fold away from viewer.

globalPartFamilies.label: Body Systems
globalPartFamilies.description: The primary structural tube or shell of a folding carton. The body is the set of panels that form the four vertical walls and the glue seam. In a standard folding carton, the body is a flat strip of four rectangular panels (front, back, two sides) plus a narrow glue tab, scored at each panel junction so the strip can be folded into a rectangular tube. The body defines L (length), W (width), H (height). All other parts attach to body panel edges or are cut from body panels.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low — rectangular panel math is straightforward. Risk increases only for angled tops (gusset roof, centered-tuck-end angled top) or skillet bodies.

globalPartFamilies.label: Glue Systems
globalPartFamilies.description: Panels or zones dedicated to creating the permanent side seam of the box tube. The glue tab is attached to one edge of the four-panel body strip and, during manufacturing, is adhered to the interior face of the opposite panel to form a closed tube. Glue zones are printed in a special color (typically cyan or magenta) in dielines to indicate no-print areas.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low — glue tab is a simple rectangle. Risk is ensuring correct width (GFW) and verifying it does not overlap structural creases.

globalPartFamilies.label: Top Closures
globalPartFamilies.description: Parts that seal the top opening of the box. These include tuck flaps (which insert into the box opening), locking flaps, tab-and-slot systems, gusset covers, and reversible lids. The top closure is attached by a structural crease to the top edge of a body panel (front or back). Companion dust flaps are hinged to the sides (side panels).
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low for standard tuck flaps. Medium for tab-slot systems (geometry of slot must match tab width). High for gusset covers and reversible lids.

globalPartFamilies.label: Bottom Closures
globalPartFamilies.description: Parts that seal the bottom opening. Types: (1) Tuck flap bottom (same as top, reversed). (2) Auto-lock / crash-lock bottom: four pre-glued flaps that snap into place when the tube is opened from flat. (3) Snap-lock bottom: two major flaps with interlocking tabs that click together without glue. (4) Full-flap bottom: one oversized flap fully covers the base. Each bottom type has specific geometry for the locking panels and minor flaps.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Medium for snap-lock (tab geometry must be precise). High for auto-lock (4-panel interlock depends on exact geometry). Expert for full-flap variant.

globalPartFamilies.label: Dust Flaps
globalPartFamilies.description: Narrow rectangular or trapezoidal panels attached to the top and bottom edges of the side panels (side-A and side-B). They fold inward before the main tuck flap or closure panel is inserted, filling the side gaps and preventing dust entry. Typically approximately W/2 wide and shorter than the tuck flap. In CefBox parameters, DFW = Dust Flap Width.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low — simple rectangles. Validation: DFW must not exceed W/2 to avoid overlap.

globalPartFamilies.label: Lock Tabs and Slots
globalPartFamilies.description: Protruding tab shapes on closure panels that insert into matching slot cutouts on an adjacent or receiver panel. Used in tab-closure tops and snap-lock bottoms. Tab shape is typically a rounded rectangle or trapezoidal tongue. Slot cutout is a rectangular or rounded-rectangle opening slightly larger than tab. The tab must be sized to require slight bending to insert (interference fit) for tamper evidence.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Medium — tab/slot sizing is critical. Too tight = hard to close. Too loose = accidental opening.

globalPartFamilies.label: Cutouts
globalPartFamilies.description: Geometry-only die cuts that remove material from a panel face without creating a new foldable face. Types: (1) Window cutout — large rectangular or shaped opening, typically backed by transparent film. (2) Circular hang hole — round punched hole in the top flap extension for peg hook display. (3) Euro-slot — elongated keyhole-shaped hole. (4) Relief notch — small semicircle at fold intersections to prevent paper stress. (5) Lock slots — narrow slots for tab insertion. Cutouts are GeometryPrimitive objects, never DielineCrease.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low for holes. Medium for windows (must maintain margin from folds). High for complex euro-slot shapes.

globalPartFamilies.label: Hang and Display Features
globalPartFamilies.description: Extensions or panels that allow the box to be hung on retail peg hooks. Types: (1) Hang hole panel — an extended rectangular panel above the top tuck flap, containing a punched circular or euro-slot hole. The panel folds flat against the box top when assembled. (2) Hang tab — a triangular or D-shaped tab die-cut and folded out from the top edge of the front or back panel. Parameters include HL (hanger length), HW (hanger width), OD (hole outer diameter), SR (slot radius).
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Medium — hole position must align with center of hang panel. Panel must not interfere with tuck flap.

globalPartFamilies.label: Handles
globalPartFamilies.description: Integrated grip features formed by folding parts of the carton. Types: (1) Folded handle — a multi-panel folded structure attached to the top of front and back panels. When folded, creates a rectangular or arch grip. Described by HL (handle length), HW (handle width), HT (handle thickness), FW1/FW2 (flap widths), SD1/SD2 (shoulder depths). (2) Arc handle — a curved arch cut from the body panel, attached by two hinge creases, folds upward to form a grip. Described by HT (height), HR (radius). (3) Handle bridge — the reinforcing double-layer structure beneath the grip opening.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: High — folded handle requires multi-panel geometry, precise anchor matching, and correct fold sequence. Arc handle requires circular geometry.

globalPartFamilies.label: Windows
globalPartFamilies.description: Rectangular or shaped cutouts in body panels intended to display the product. A transparent film is adhered on the interior side. Described by WL (window length), WH (window height), WR (window corner radius). Windows must maintain minimum margins from all panel edges (folds and cuts). Windows are GeometryPrimitive objects. They do not create structural creases.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low geometrically. Medium in validation (margin from edges must be enforced).

globalPartFamilies.label: Tear and Perforation Features
globalPartFamilies.description: Perforated or scored lines that allow the consumer to easily open the box by tearing along a defined path. The tear strip is a narrow band (typically 5–10mm wide) running horizontally around the box perimeter between two perforation lines. One end has a pull tab or notch. In the flat dieline, the tear strip appears as two parallel perforation lines on all four body panels. Parameters: EXD (extra depth), R1/R2/R3 (radii for tear notch geometry), GFA (glue flap angle).
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Medium — perforation line rendering and tear-pull-tab geometry require special tooling representation in DXF.

globalPartFamilies.label: Dividers, Inserts, and Partitions
globalPartFamilies.description: Panels that fold inward from the body to create internal compartments or product-holding structures. Types: (1) Centered divider — a panel attached to one side panel, folds across the interior parallel to front/back panels, divides box into 2 equal compartments. Height equals interior height. (2) Integrated partitions — two perpendicular divider panels attached to opposite body panels, creating 6 cells (2×3 grid). (3) Built-in inserts — flaps extending from side panels, folding inward to grip the product from above and below. Parameters: PD1/PD2 (partition depth), D1–D6 (insert dimensions), DL (divider length).
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: High — internal panels must fold correctly without conflicting with body panels. Verification with 3D folding simulation strongly recommended.

globalPartFamilies.label: Mount Structures
globalPartFamilies.description: Extended tabs or panels on side walls that fold inward and interlock to create a cradle or platform that holds the product in a fixed position. Formed by tucking the extended portion of two side walls (one from each side), creating a shelf or mount surface at a defined height inside the box. Parameters: D1, D2 (mount height and depth).
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Very high — mount geometry depends on precise side-wall extensions and slot geometry. Must prototype before production.

globalPartFamilies.label: Reversible Lids
globalPartFamilies.description: A top closure mechanism where the lid panel can be rotated 180° (reversed) to open the box. When closed, the lid tucks down the front face. When opened, the lid flips and stands up, revealing the product. The lid is a panel attached to the back panel top edge by a structural crease. It contains an insert slot where an inner tab panel locks it closed. Used in skillet-style cartons for cigarette/gum-style packaging.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Very high — hinge geometry, insert slot position, and lid depth are all critical. Exact replication requires physical prototype.

globalPartFamilies.label: Skillet / Tray Structures
globalPartFamilies.description: Skillet-end cartons (also called skillets or skillet boxes) differ from standard tuck-end boxes in that the end closure panels are angled or the body ratio is significantly wider than deep, creating a tray-like profile. The skillet body is typically landscape orientation (L > H). The side walls are shallow. Used for cigarettes, gum, cookies. The skillet may have a separate lid or an integrated reversible lid.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: High — body aspect ratio and shallow side walls create unusual fold geometry.

globalPartFamilies.label: Gusset Roof and Gusset Cover Structures
globalPartFamilies.description: Gusset panels are angled or pleated panels that allow a flat surface to transition into an angled roof or expand to cover a wider opening. (1) Gusset roof — the top of the box is formed by two angled panels meeting at a ridge, with triangular gusset panels at each end filling the corners. Creates a tent/house roof profile. (2) Gusset cover — a tuck-end cover with reinforced corner gussets providing structural stiffness. The gusset panels are typically triangular, folded in as part of the cover assembly.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Very high — gusset geometry requires precise angular calculations. Fold sequence is non-obvious.

globalPartFamilies.label: Guide and Print Helpers
globalPartFamilies.description: Non-structural geometry that helps printers, designers, and engineers work with the dieline. Includes: (1) Bleed area — typically 3mm extension beyond cut line on printable panels. (2) Safe area — typically 5mm inset from cut line where no important content should be placed. (3) Score lines / fold guides — dashed lines indicating valley folds. (4) Glue zone — hatched or colored area indicating where adhesive is applied (typically the glue tab and auto-lock bottom glue panels). (5) No-print zone — area where adhesive or mechanical features prevent print. All are GeometryPrimitive objects.
globalPartFamilies.implementationRisk: Low — purely visual/informational. No structural impact.

body-strip.label: Standard 4-Panel Body Strip
body-strip.description: The core rectangular body of a standard folding carton. Consists of four rectangular panels (front, back, side-A, side-B) joined in a horizontal strip by three vertical structural creases (score lines). A narrow glue tab is attached to one end. In the flat dieline layout the total unfolded width = L + W + L + W + GFW, and total height = H (plus top and bottom flap extensions). When the glue tab is adhered to the back panel interior, the strip forms a rectangular tube. The four structural creases become the four vertical box corners.
body-strip.role: Primary structural shell. All other parts attach to its top/bottom edges or are cut from its interior.

inputs.name: L
inputs.label: Length
inputs.description: Interior length of box (longest horizontal dimension)

inputs.name: W
inputs.label: Width
inputs.description: Interior width of box (shortest horizontal dimension / depth)

inputs.name: H
inputs.label: Height
inputs.description: Interior height of box

inputs.name: T
inputs.label: Material Thickness
inputs.description: Caliper of board. Used for inner-to-outer dimension conversion.

inputs.name: GFW
inputs.label: Glue Flap Width
inputs.description: Width of glue seam tab
inputs.calculationNote: Must be wide enough for adhesive but not so wide it shows through the box opening. Typical = 12mm.

faces.label: Back Panel
faces.position: mirror of front, separated by side-B

faces.label: Glue Tab
faces.note: This is the manufacturing seam. Not visible on finished box.

structuralCreases.label: Front/SideA Vertical Crease
structuralCreases.position: x = W (from left edge of dieline)

body-strip.geometryBehavior: The dieline unfolds as a horizontal strip. Panel order left to right: [glue-tab | back | side-B | front | side-A]. Note: some templates reverse the order. The total flat dieline width = GFW + L + W + L + W. Total height at body level = H. Top and bottom parts extend above and below the H zone.
validationRules: L must be > 0
W must be > 0, W must be <= L (by convention, L is always the longer dimension)
H must be > 0
GFW must be >= 8mm and <= 20mm for typical packaging
No panel width may be zero or negative
body-strip.3dFoldingNotes: Fold sequence: (1) Fold crease between front and side-A 90° inward. (2) Fold crease between front and side-B 90° inward. (3) Wrap back panel to meet glue tab. (4) Apply glue to tab and press to interior of back panel. Result: a flat-collapsed tube. To erect: push corners outward simultaneously.
body-strip.artworkNotes: All four panels (front, back, side-A, side-B) are printable. Glue tab is non-printable (covered by adhesive). Bleed extends 3mm beyond cut lines on all printable panel edges.
productionRisks: Grain direction of board must be parallel to H dimension for best fold quality
Material thickness compensation affects final inner vs outer dimension — always confirm inner vs outer mode

sleeve-body.label: Sleeve Body (Two-Panel Strip)
sleeve-body.description: A body made of only front and back panels (2 wide panels + glue tab), forming a flat sleeve. Used in skillet-type boxes where the box is shallow and wide. The sleeve folds flat naturally and is erected by pushing the ends open. The side walls in a skillet configuration are the closure panels themselves.

inputs.name: L
inputs.label: Length
inputs.description: Outer length of skillet box

inputs.name: W
inputs.label: Width
inputs.description: Outer width / depth of skillet box

inputs.name: H
inputs.label: Height
inputs.description: Outer height of skillet box

sleeve-body.geometryBehavior: Flat strip: [glue-tab | back | front]. Width = GFW + L + L.
validationRules: L > W for skillet (landscape orientation)
sleeve-body.3dFoldingNotes: Fold front panel over back panel. Apply glue to tab. Result: flat collapsed sleeve. Erect by pulling top and bottom edges apart — the end closure panels form the sides.
sleeve-body.artworkNotes: Front and back panels are printable. Skillet boxes often have narrow side closure panels that are visible in display.
productionRisks: Skillet requires precise end closure geometry for automated filling line compatibility

side-glue-tab.label: Side Glue Tab
side-glue-tab.description: A narrow vertical panel attached to one end of the body strip. Its outer edge is a straight cut line. Its inner edge (hinge) is a structural crease. During manufacturing the glue tab is coated with adhesive and pressed against the interior face of the opposite body panel, creating the permanent side seam. The tab must be wide enough for reliable adhesion (minimum 10mm) but narrow enough not to be visible through the open top/bottom. Standard width range: 10–15mm.
side-glue-tab.role: Creates the permanent seam that closes the body strip into a tube
attachesTo: panel-sideB (or panel-front for some skillet configurations)

inputs.name: GFW
inputs.label: Glue Flap Width
inputs.description: Width of the glue tab from hinge crease to cut edge

geometryPrimitives.label: Glue Zone Rectangle
geometryPrimitives.purpose: Visual indicator in dieline — printed in special color to indicate adhesive zone

anchors.position: vertical line at hinge between sideB and glue tab

side-glue-tab.geometryBehavior: Simple rectangle of width GFW and height H. Left edge is the hinge crease. Right edge is the cut line.
validationRules: GFW >= 10mm
GFW <= 20mm
Height must equal body height H
No print content in glue zone
side-glue-tab.3dFoldingNotes: The glue tab is the last panel to be glued in factory pre-gluing. It stays glued permanently — the finished box never separates here.
side-glue-tab.artworkNotes: Mark as NO-PRINT ZONE in artwork guidelines. Dieline representation: hatched rectangle.
productionRisks: Glue tab must have adequate dwell time under pressure for adhesive to cure

reverse-tuck-flap.label: Reverse Tuck Flap
reverse-tuck-flap.description: A tuck flap where the top flap (attached to back panel) tucks into the box from the front opening direction, and the bottom flap (attached to front panel) tucks into the box from the back direction. Therefore top and bottom tucks enter from OPPOSITE sides (reverse of each other). This is the most common pharmaceutical and general product carton style. The tuck flap geometry: rectangular base (width = L, depth = TFW) with an angled or rounded leading edge. A small triangular lock notch on each side of the flap catches on the dust flap corner to hold the closure closed. TFR (tuck flap radius) is the corner radius of the leading edge. TFW = tuck flap width (depth of insertion).
reverse-tuck-flap.role: Top closure that inserts from the reverse (front) direction

inputs.name: TFW
inputs.label: Tuck Flap Width (insertion depth)
inputs.description: How deep the tuck flap inserts into the box opening
inputs.calculationNote: TFW should be >= W/2 + 5mm to ensure secure closure. Typically W * 0.6 to W * 0.8.

inputs.name: TFR
inputs.label: Tuck Flap Radius
inputs.description: Corner radius on the leading edge of the tuck flap

inputs.name: DFW
inputs.label: Dust Flap Width
inputs.description: Width of companion dust flaps on side panels

faces.label: Top Tuck Flap Panel
faces.note: Leading edge has radius TFR at corners. Side edges have small notch cutouts for locking.

structuralCreases.label: Top Tuck Flap Hinge
structuralCreases.position: horizontal line at top of back panel body zone

anchors.position: bottom edge of tuck flap panel = top edge of back panel

reverse-tuck-flap.geometryBehavior: The tuck flap is a rectangular panel of width L and height TFW, attached at its base by a crease to the top of the back panel. Its leading edge (top in flat dieline) has two corner radii of TFR. At each side, a triangular notch protrudes outward by approximately 2–3mm — this notch catches on the inside edge of the dust flap when the box is closed. The lock notch position from the side edge = approximately DFW (must align with dust flap edge when closed).
validationRules: TFW >= 12mm
TFW <= W * 0.9 (must not exceed box width or it will buckle)
TFR >= 2mm
Notch position from side = DFW ± 2mm
Tuck flap base edge width must equal L exactly
reverse-tuck-flap.3dFoldingNotes: When assembling: (1) Fold dust flaps (side panels) inward 90°. (2) Fold tuck flap (attached to back panel) 90° over the dust flaps. (3) Push tuck flap downward into box opening. The lock notches snap behind the dust flap inner edges. To open: press inward on both sides of tuck flap near base to release notches, then pull flap outward.
reverse-tuck-flap.artworkNotes: Top tuck flap is a printable panel — visible from the top when box is open. It carries branding on its exterior surface. Interior face may show through window if box has window.
productionRisks: TFW too long: flap buckles inside box. TFW too short: flap does not lock securely
Notch size too large: structural weakness. Too small: hard to open
TFR must match die capability (minimum 2mm for most dies)

straight-tuck-flap.label: Straight Tuck Flap
straight-tuck-flap.description: A tuck flap where BOTH the top and bottom flaps tuck into the box from the SAME direction (typically both entering from the front). This is the straight tuck style. Geometry is identical to the reverse tuck flap, but the assembly direction reverses one of the closures. In CefBox straightTuckEnd: the top flap attached to the back panel and the bottom flap also attached to the back panel (or both attached to front panel — depending on implementation). The result is both closures are on the same side of the box when assembled.
straight-tuck-flap.role: Top and bottom closure, both entering from same face
straight-tuck-flap.geometryBehavior: Same geometry as reverse-tuck-flap. Difference is only in which panel (front vs back) they are attached to, determining the insertion direction.
validationRules: Same as reverse-tuck-flap
straight-tuck-flap.3dFoldingNotes: Both closures enter from the same face. This means to open the box fully, both ends are accessible from one direction — ideal for products inserted from either end during filling.
straight-tuck-flap.artworkNotes: Straight tuck is preferred when products are loaded from a consistent direction on automated lines.
productionRisks: Both closures on same side creates slightly asymmetric appearance on finished box — confirm with client

centered-tuck-flap.label: Centered / Angled Tuck Flap
centered-tuck-flap.description: A tuck flap with a center-peaked or angled leading edge. Instead of a flat or rounded leading edge, the flap has a triangular peak at the center (like an inverted V shape) or a stepped profile. This is used in templates with angled-top aesthetics (e.g., centered-tuck-end-carton). The angle creates a visually distinctive top when viewed from the front. Parameters: D1 (angle rise at center, i.e., the height of the peak above the flap base), D2 (second dimension for angled geometry).

inputs.name: D1
inputs.label: Angle Rise
inputs.description: Height of center peak above flap base line

centered-tuck-flap.geometryBehavior: The flap base (hinge line) has width = L. The leading edge rises to a point or stepped profile. The exact polygon depends on D1 and D2 values. TFR applies to corner transitions.
validationRules: D1 must be positive
TFW1 must be >= W/2
centered-tuck-flap.3dFoldingNotes: Angled top is purely aesthetic. Folding is the same as a straight tuck. The peak sits above the box top face creating a distinctive silhouette.
centered-tuck-flap.artworkNotes: The angled flap face is prominently visible when boxed product is on shelf — key branding surface.
productionRisks: Complex leading edge requires precise die — verify die accuracy before large run

locking-lip-flap.label: Locking Lip / Catalog Lock Tab Flap
locking-lip-flap.description: A top or bottom closure that uses a tab projecting from the primary flap which inserts into a slot cut into the body panel below/above it. This creates a stronger closure than a simple tuck flap — requires deliberate action to open and resists accidental opening. Used in 'with-locking-tab-on-top-and-bottom', 'snap-lock-bottom-carton-with-tab-closure', 'auto-lock-bottom-carton-with-tab-closure', 'with-handle'. Parameters: TL (tab length — how far tab protrudes), TR (tab radius — corner rounding of tab), TD1 (tab depth 1 — primary), TD2 (tab depth 2 — secondary step), PR (punch radius of slot ends).
locking-lip-flap.role: Secure snap-tab closure for top panel

inputs.name: TL
inputs.label: Tab Length
inputs.description: Total length of the locking tab (full width it spans)

inputs.name: TR
inputs.label: Tab Radius
inputs.description: Corner radius of tab ends

inputs.name: TD1
inputs.label: Tab Depth 1
inputs.description: Primary insertion depth of tab into slot

inputs.name: TD2
inputs.label: Tab Depth 2
inputs.description: Secondary step depth if tab is stepped

inputs.name: PR
inputs.label: Punch Radius
inputs.description: Radius of the slot end punch — relieves stress at slot corners

faces.label: Locking Flap Panel
faces.note: The flap panel width = L, height includes the flap body (TFW) plus the projecting tab (TD1)

structuralCreases.description: Hinge at top of front panel (or back panel for bottom closure)

geometryPrimitives.label: Lock Slot Cutout
geometryPrimitives.position: On the body panel into which the tab inserts — typically on the back panel just below top edge
geometryPrimitives.description: This slot is cut into the body panel — it is a geometry-only feature (GeometryPrimitive), NOT a crease or face

locking-lip-flap.geometryBehavior: The flap panel extends from the top of the front panel. The lower portion (height TFW) is the dust-sealing flap body. The tab (height TD1) protrudes further down from the flap. When the flap is closed, the body covers the box top and the tab pushes through the slot cut in the back panel (or into the box interior through a slot at the top edge of the back panel). The lock slot is positioned on the back panel, centered, width TL + clearance. The two rounded ends of the slot are created by punch radius PR.
validationRules: TL must be <= L - 20mm (must leave at least 10mm margins on each side)
TD1 must be >= 5mm
PR >= 1.5mm
Slot must not fall within 5mm of any crease line
Tab width (TL) must be slightly less than slot width to allow insertion
locking-lip-flap.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Fold dust flaps inward. (2) Fold locking flap down over box top. (3) Press tab through slot in front face. Tab bends and snaps into box interior. (4) To open: push tab back through slot from inside (or use finger notch if provided).
locking-lip-flap.artworkNotes: The flap exterior is a key visible surface. The slot cut in the body panel should be positioned where it does not interfere with primary branding area.
productionRisks: Slot too tight = hard to assemble
PR too small = paper tears at slot corner
Tab too long = difficult to insert without tools

dust-flap.label: Standard Dust Flap
dust-flap.description: A rectangular panel attached by a horizontal structural crease to the top (or bottom) edge of a side panel (side-A or side-B). Dust flaps fold inward 90° before the main closure flap is applied, filling the side gaps to prevent dust ingress and provide structural support to the closure assembly. Width of dust flap = DFW (typically W/2 - 2mm to allow the tuck flap to slide over them). Height = H but this is the 'depth' of the flap (extension above body). In the flat dieline, dust flaps appear as small rectangles attached to the top and bottom edges of both side panels.
dust-flap.role: Side gap filler at top/bottom openings, provides support for main closure panel

inputs.name: DFW
inputs.label: Dust Flap Width
inputs.description: Depth of dust flap (how far it extends inward when folded)
inputs.typicalCalculation: DFW = W/2 - 2mm to 3mm clearance for smooth closure. Must not extend past the centerline of box interior.

dust-flap.geometryBehavior: Simple rectangles attached to top and bottom of side panels. In the flat dieline, they are above and below the body H zone at the side panel positions. Width = W (matches side panel width). Height = DFW.
validationRules: DFW >= 8mm
DFW <= W/2 (critical — two dust flaps from opposite sides must not overlap when folded in)
DFW must not interfere with snap-lock or auto-lock bottom mechanism geometry
dust-flap.3dFoldingNotes: Fold dust flaps 90° inward FIRST before the main tuck/lock flap. They create a platform for the closure panel to rest on.
dust-flap.artworkNotes: Dust flaps are interior surfaces — typically not printed. Small corner relief cuts may appear where dust flap hinge meets body panel crease (corner relief notch).
productionRisks: DFW at exact W/2 causes jam when both flaps touch — always use W/2 minus clearance

auto-lock-bottom-panel.label: Auto-Lock (Crash-Lock) Bottom Panel Assembly
auto-lock-bottom-panel.description: The auto-lock bottom (also called crash-lock, auto-bottom, or snap-lock bottom in some industries) is a set of four bottom closure panels that are pre-glued in the factory while flat, then spring open when the box tube is erected. It consists of: (1) Two major bottom flaps attached to front and back panels, each with diagonal glue scores. (2) Two minor flaps attached to side panels. When the flat box is pushed open, the four flaps automatically interlock. No manual assembly required. The bottom is completely secure once erected. The diagonal scores on the major flaps allow the characteristic 'crush and flatten' movement. The bottom cannot easily be re-flattened after erection.
auto-lock-bottom-panel.role: Fast-erecting, secure bottom closure — ideal for automated box erection lines

inputs.name: GFW
inputs.label: Glue Flap Width
inputs.description: Width of the auto-lock glue panel (the pre-glued minor panel that holds the assembly)

inputs.name: DFW
inputs.label: Bottom Flap Minor Width
inputs.description: Depth of the minor bottom flaps on side panels

faces.label: Major Bottom Flap (Front)
faces.note: This flap extends to approximately W/2 + 5mm. It has diagonal score lines starting from approximately 10mm in from each corner.

faces.label: Auto-Lock Glue Panel
faces.note: Pre-glued to the interior of the opposite major flap in factory. Creates the interlocked spring.

structuralCreases.label: Diagonal Score Left Front
structuralCreases.description: Diagonal crease on major front flap from approximately (0, 0) to (10, W/2) — creates fold along which the spring mechanism works

geometryPrimitives.label: Auto-Lock Pre-Glue Zone
geometryPrimitives.description: Zone where factory glue is applied. Connects glue panel to opposite major flap.

auto-lock-bottom-panel.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline, all four bottom flaps extend below the body H zone. The major flaps (front, back) are larger rectangles with diagonal internal scores. The minor flaps (sides) are smaller. The auto-lock glue panel is an additional small panel attached to one major flap's edge by a crease. The geometric key is the diagonal crease positions — typically at 45° from the flap corner, starting approximately at x = W/4 from the side crease. Exact position depends on W and L ratio.
validationRules: Major flap height >= W/2 + 3mm overlap for secure bottom
Diagonal crease angle must be calculated from exact W and L to ensure flat collapse
Glue panel width GFW must allow adhesive coverage >= 10mm
Minor flap height must be < W/2 (to nest inside major flaps)
auto-lock-bottom-panel.3dFoldingNotes: Factory assembly: (1) Box is flat. (2) The auto-lock glue panel is glued to the interior surface of the opposite major flap while flat. (3) The diagonal scores allow the assembly to be re-flattened for shipping. (4) When user erects box: push tube open — the four flaps spring outward and lock into rectangular base. No further action needed.
auto-lock-bottom-panel.artworkNotes: Bottom exterior is partially visible on shelf (bottom facing). Large flat outer surface of major flap suitable for barcode, batch code, expiry date. The glue panel is interior — not printable.
productionRisks: Diagonal score angle critical — wrong angle = bottom doesn't fully collapse flat or doesn't pop open reliably
Pre-glue zone must be precise — too narrow = bottom opens under load; too wide = flap doesn't fold correctly
This is the most mechanically complex common part — high verification need

snap-lock-bottom-panel.label: Snap-Lock Bottom Panel Assembly
snap-lock-bottom-panel.description: The snap-lock bottom is a manually assembled bottom closure consisting of two major bottom flaps that interlock without glue. One major flap has a trapezoidal or rounded tongue that inserts into a slot in the other major flap. The interlocked flaps cannot be pulled apart without deliberate force. Minor dust flaps from the side panels fold in first. This system requires manual assembly but provides a strong, reclosable base. Used when auto-lock tooling is unavailable or for smaller production runs.
snap-lock-bottom-panel.role: Manually assembled interlocking bottom closure without adhesive

inputs.name: DFW
inputs.label: Dust/Minor Flap Width
inputs.description: W/2 - clearance

faces.label: Snap Lock Major Flap A
faces.note: Contains the tongue/tab that inserts into the slot

geometryPrimitives.label: Snap Lock Slot
geometryPrimitives.position: center of major flap B, parallel to fold edge
geometryPrimitives.description: The slot in major flap B into which the tongue of major flap A inserts

snap-lock-bottom-panel.geometryBehavior: Major flap A has a tongue/tab protruding from its free edge. Major flap B has a slot cut parallel to its fold edge. When assembling: (1) fold minor flaps in; (2) fold major flap B in; (3) fold major flap A in and push its tongue through slot in B. Tongue bends under B and locks.
validationRules: Tongue width < slot width by exactly 1mm clearance
Tongue depth <= 8mm to fit through slot without excessive force
Slot must be >= 5mm from fold crease
Minor flap height < W/2
snap-lock-bottom-panel.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly order: (1) Dust/minor flaps fold in first. (2) Major flap B (with slot) folds in. (3) Major flap A (with tongue) folds in last, tongue pushes through slot and snaps flat beneath flap B. (4) Tongue holds flap assembly closed under load.
snap-lock-bottom-panel.artworkNotes: Bottom exterior visible. Slot cutout visible on bottom exterior — consider placement relative to barcode/branding.
productionRisks: Tongue too wide or long = hard assembly for consumer
Slot too large = bottom opens accidentally under light load
Clearances must be material-thickness aware

full-flap-bottom-panel.label: Full-Flap Bottom Panel
full-flap-bottom-panel.description: An auto-lock (crash-lock) bottom where ONE of the major flaps is extended to the full width of the box (width = L), completely covering the entire exterior base. Standard auto-lock has two major flaps that each cover half the base, leaving a seam line down the center. The full-flap variant extends one major flap to cover the entire bottom, giving a clean, uninterrupted exterior base surface. The other major flap becomes an interior support flap. Parameters: TFW (top flap), TFR (top flap radius), GFW, DFW.
full-flap-bottom-panel.role: Premium auto-lock bottom with clean uninterrupted exterior base surface

faces.label: Full-Width Outer Bottom Flap
faces.note: Extends entire base width, has diagonal scores and glue panel

full-flap-bottom-panel.geometryBehavior: Same as auto-lock but one major flap height = W instead of W/2. The diagonal score angles change accordingly. Single uninterrupted exterior base when assembled.
validationRules: Full flap height >= W + 2mm
Diagonal score angles recalculated for W (not W/2)
full-flap-bottom-panel.3dFoldingNotes: Same erection behavior as auto-lock. The full-width flap folds first, then the inner support flap nests inside it. Result: continuous exterior base.
full-flap-bottom-panel.artworkNotes: Full-width exterior base provides maximum area for barcode/branding on bottom. Premium appearance justified for cosmetics/luxury goods.
productionRisks: Full flap diagonal score geometry is non-standard — requires careful calculation and die verification

circular-hang-hole.label: Circular Hang Hole
circular-hang-hole.description: A circular punched hole cut into the hang hole panel extension above the top tuck flap. Used to hang the box on a retail peg hook (euro-hook or standard peg). The hang hole is purely a cutout — it creates no face, no crease, and no fold. It is a GeometryPrimitive circle. Located at the vertical center of the hang panel extension and horizontally centered on the top panel (front or back). Hole diameter is specified by OD (outer diameter). A smaller reinforcement ring may optionally be present. The hang hole panel extension height is HL (hanger length). HW (hanger width) refers to the width of the hang panel which equals L (front panel width).
requiredAnchors: top of tuck flap panel (hang extension above it)

inputs.name: HL
inputs.label: Hanger Length (panel extension height)
inputs.description: Height of the rectangular panel extension above the tuck flap that contains the hole

inputs.name: HW
inputs.label: Hanger Width
inputs.description: Width of hang extension = L (front panel width)

inputs.name: OD
inputs.label: Hole Outer Diameter
inputs.description: Diameter of the punch hole
inputs.standard: 6mm standard euro-slot, or 8mm/10mm for larger hooks

faces.label: Hang Hole Panel Extension
faces.note: This IS a face/panel because it folds as part of the tuck flap assembly and is glued double-thick for strength

geometryPrimitives.label: Circular Hang Hole
geometryPrimitives.position: centered horizontally at x = L/2, vertically at y = HL/2 from top edge of hang extension
geometryPrimitives.description: Pure cutout — removes material. No face created. GeometryPrimitive only.

circular-hang-hole.geometryBehavior: The hang panel extension appears in the flat dieline as a rectangular extension above the top tuck flap. When the box is assembled, the tuck flap folds down and the hang extension protrudes above the box top. The circular hole punches through both layers (tuck flap and hang extension are glued together for strength). Position: center of circle at (L/2, HL/2) from extension top-left corner.
validationRules: OD >= 5mm (minimum for standard peg hooks)
OD <= 12mm
Hole must maintain 5mm minimum margin from all cut edges and fold lines
Hole center must be >= OD/2 + 5mm from top edge
circular-hang-hole.3dFoldingNotes: The hang extension is double-layered in the assembled box (tuck flap glued to hang extension). The hole is through both layers. When the box hangs on a peg, the weight is distributed across both layers.
circular-hang-hole.artworkNotes: The hang extension exterior is a printed surface — shows product name/logo on retail peg display. Consider printing on both the extension and the interior surface (visible when tuck flap opens).
productionRisks: Single-layer hang hole may tear under product weight — ensure double-layer or reinforcement ring
Hole position must be at exact center or box will tilt on peg hook

hang-tab.label: Hang Tab
hang-tab.description: A hang tab is a rectangular or D-shaped extension attached to the top edge of the tuck flap, containing a slot-shaped hang hole. Unlike the circular hang hole on a panel extension, the hang tab is a folded structure: the tab folds 90° forward/outward from the tuck flap face, creating a double-thickness tab that protrudes above the box top. The slot in the hang tab allows it to hang on a euro hook. Parameters: SL (slot length), SW (slot width), FR (slot fillet radius), SAL (slot anchor length), TFW1 (tuck flap primary width), TW (tab width), OD1 (slot outer dimension 1).
hang-tab.role: Folded double-thickness retail hang tab attached to top of tuck flap

faces.label: Hang Tab Inner Half
faces.note: Attaches to top edge of tuck flap

faces.label: Hang Tab Outer Half
faces.note: Folds 180° to double up against inner half

structuralCreases.description: Horizontal crease at midpoint of tab — outer half folds back onto inner half

geometryPrimitives.label: Euro Slot
geometryPrimitives.position: centered on tab, positioned so slot center is in upper half of folded tab

hang-tab.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline, the hang tab appears as an extension above the tuck flap, centered horizontally. It has a fold crease at the midpoint. The euro-slot is cut through the upper half (which becomes the front face when folded). The lower half folds back and adheres to the upper half, creating a reinforced double-layer tab. The slot spans across the fold so both layers are punched.
validationRules: Tab width TW must be sufficient for euro-slot (TW >= SL + 8mm on each side)
SAL must be sufficient for hook insertion (SAL >= SL/2 + 5mm above slot)
Slot must maintain 4mm margin from tab edges
hang-tab.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: the outer tab half folds 180° back onto inner half (folds at crease). The two halves are glued together. The euro slot punches through both layers providing strong hanging support.
hang-tab.artworkNotes: The hang tab is the most visible part on a peg display. Both front and back faces are printable.
productionRisks: Tab must be centered on tuck flap or box tilts
Euro-slot position relative to fold crease is critical — must punch both layers simultaneously

folded-handle.label: Folded Handle Assembly
folded-handle.description: An integrated grip handle formed by multiple panels that fold out of the top of the box body (extending above the top closure). The handle structure is attached to both the front and back panels. It consists of: (1) Two 'shoulder' panels (one on front, one on back) that form the sides of the handle arch. (2) A 'bridge' panel at the top that forms the grip surface. (3) A 'slot' die cut in the bridge through which fingers reach. (4) A 'palm pad' panel that doubles the grip for comfort. The handle dimensions: HL (handle length = span between shoulders), HW (handle width = width of bridge), HT (handle thickness = depth of arch), FW1/FW2 (flap widths), SD1/SD2 (shoulder depths = height of handle walls), SR (slot radius), TD1/TD2 (top dimensions), PR (punch radius). This is a catalog lock top type — the handle incorporates the top closure.
folded-handle.role: Integrated carry handle and top closure in one assembly

inputs.name: HL
inputs.label: Handle Length
inputs.description: The clear span of the handle opening (finger slot width)

inputs.name: HW
inputs.label: Handle Width
inputs.description: Width of the bridge panel (palm grip width)

inputs.name: HT
inputs.label: Handle Thickness
inputs.description: Depth of handle arch above box top

inputs.name: SR
inputs.label: Slot Radius
inputs.description: Radius of finger slot corners

faces.label: Front Shoulder Panel
faces.description: Attached to front panel top edge

faces.label: Back Shoulder Panel
faces.description: Attached to back panel top edge

faces.label: Handle Bridge Panel
faces.description: Grip surface connecting two shoulder panels

faces.label: Palm Pad (inner reinforcement)
faces.description: Folds over bridge for double-thickness grip

geometryPrimitives.label: Finger Slot Cutout
geometryPrimitives.description: The cutout through which fingers grip. NOT a face. GeometryPrimitive only.

folded-handle.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline, the handle assembly appears as a complex multi-panel structure above both the front and back panels. The exact fold sequence and panel arrangement depends heavily on parameters. The handle bridge spans across and is attached to shoulder panels on each side. The palm pad folds 180° onto the bridge. The locking tab system (catalog lock) secures the handle assembly closed and simultaneously seals the box top.
validationRules: HL >= 40mm (minimum for adult fingers)
HT >= 15mm (minimum handle height for grip)
SR >= 8mm (finger comfort minimum)
Handle must clear box top edge when erect
Bridge width must span from front to back panel plus margin
folded-handle.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Fold shoulder panels up 90° from front/back panels. (2) Fold bridge panel horizontally connecting the shoulders. (3) Fold palm pad over bridge. (4) Insert locking tab through slot. Handle stands erect above box top. The handle carries the box weight — the shoulder-to-panel hinges bear load.
folded-handle.artworkNotes: The handle exterior (bridge outer face) is prominently visible during carrying — key branding position. The inner palm pad is hidden when assembled.
productionRisks: Handle geometry is the most mechanically complex part — requires physical prototype before production
Finger slot radius SR must be large enough to prevent paper cuts
Handle must support product weight — verify with material/caliper specification

arc-handle.label: Arc Handle
arc-handle.description: A simplified arch-shaped handle created by die cutting an arch shape from the front and back panels of the box, connected at the top by a crease. The arch cutout removes material from the panel to create a grip opening. The material above the arch hinge folds outward to form the grip. Unlike the folded handle (which is a separate assembly), the arc handle is integral to the body panels — it is cut and scored directly into the front and back panels. Parameters: HT (arc height = height of arch opening), HR (arch radius = radius of the arch curve).
arc-handle.role: Simple integrated carry handle cut from body panels

inputs.name: HT
inputs.label: Arc Height
inputs.description: Vertical height of the arch opening

inputs.name: HR
inputs.label: Arc Radius
inputs.description: Radius of the arch curve

inputs.name: SR
inputs.label: Slot Radius
inputs.description: Radius of cut corners for comfort

faces.label: Arc Handle Grip Panel
faces.description: The material remaining above the arch hinge line. Folds outward 90° from the box face to form the grip bar.

structuralCreases.label: Arc Handle Hinge Crease
structuralCreases.description: Horizontal score line at bottom of handle grip, parallel to box top edge. This is the fold line from which the grip panel extends outward.

geometryPrimitives.label: Arc Handle Cutout
geometryPrimitives.description: The arched cutout below the grip panel. Both front and back panels have matching arches. When the grip panels on both faces fold outward they interlock or are held together, forming a carry arch over the box top. GeometryPrimitive — material removed.

arc-handle.geometryBehavior: The arc cutout appears on both front and back panels, centered horizontally. The arch shape is a half-ellipse or half-circle of radius HR and height HT. The grip panel (above the hinge) extends from the top of the arch to the top edge of the body panel. When folded: both grip panels on front and back lean toward each other and interlock at the top, forming an arch bridge over the box top.
validationRules: HR must be large enough for comfortable finger grip (HR >= H * 0.15)
Arc must maintain >= 10mm margin from side creases
Arc cutout must not exceed 60% of panel width
arc-handle.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: the grip panels on front and back fold outward simultaneously and interlock at their tips. The box top is open between the two arches — product is inserted first, then handle assembled.
arc-handle.artworkNotes: Arc cut creates visible opening on front and back faces — design must account for the arch negative space in artwork.
productionRisks: The interlocking at the arch top must be designed carefully — otherwise handle collapses under load
Front and back arch cutouts must be identical and aligned

window-cutout.label: Window Cutout
window-cutout.description: A rectangular, oval, or shaped cutout in a body panel that allows the product to be seen. Typically backed by a transparent polypropylene or PET film adhered to the interior of the panel. The window is a pure GeometryPrimitive — it removes material and creates no face or crease. Parameters: WL (window length), WH (window height), WR (window corner radius). Multiple windows per template are indexed (WL1/WH1, WL2/WH2, etc.).
window-cutout.role: Product visibility cutout backed by transparent film
attachesTo: panel-front (or panel-back, or both side panels)

inputs.name: WR
inputs.label: Window Corner Radius
inputs.description: Radius of rounded rectangle corners

geometryPrimitives.label: Window Cutout Shape
geometryPrimitives.description: Material removed from panel. No face. No crease. GeometryPrimitive only.

window-cutout.geometryBehavior: Window is positioned within a panel face. Center position is typically centered horizontally on the panel and vertically at mid-height. Minimum margin from panel edges: 10mm from fold creases, 8mm from cut edges. Multiple windows: indexed with separate WL/WH parameters per window.
validationRules: WL + 2*margin <= panel width
WH + 2*margin <= panel height
Window must not overlap any fold crease
Window must not overlap glue zone
WR >= 2mm
window-cutout.3dFoldingNotes: Windows are cut before the box is erected. Transparent film is applied in manufacturing. Window maintains its cutout shape in 3D assembled box.
window-cutout.artworkNotes: Window area should be marked as 'clear film zone' in artwork templates. Artwork behind the window (on the product itself) may show through and should be considered in design.
productionRisks: Film adhesive must bond securely — specify film lamination parameters
Window margins from creases must be respected — paper near folds is weakened

tear-strip.label: Tear Strip / Perforated Opening Strip
tear-strip.description: A tamper-evident opening feature consisting of two parallel perforation lines running around the box perimeter (across all four panels at a defined height above the bottom closure). Between the perforations is a narrow strip of material (typically 5–10mm wide) with a pull-tab notch at one end. Consumer tears the pull tab and the strip separates from the box, opening the top portion. The pull tab is a small triangular or rectangular notch that protrudes outward from the perforation line at one corner of one panel. Parameters: EXD (extra depth = height from bottom edge to lower perforation line), R1 (radius of upper perforations), R2 (radius of lower perforations), R3 (radius of tear notch), GFA (glue flap angle = angle of the glue flap cut at the glue seam, typically 45°).
attachesTo: all four body panels at defined height
requiredAnchors: continuous horizontal band across all panels

inputs.name: EXD
inputs.label: Extra Depth (position from bottom)
inputs.description: Distance from bottom edge to the lower perforation line. Sets the position of the tear strip on the box.

inputs.name: GFA
inputs.label: Glue Flap Angle
inputs.description: Angle of glue tab cut at tear strip location — the glue tab must be angled at the tear zone so the strip separates cleanly at the glue seam too.

geometryPrimitives.label: Upper Perforation Line
geometryPrimitives.description: Horizontal dashed cut line across all four panels at height EXD + strip_width from bottom

geometryPrimitives.label: Lower Perforation Line
geometryPrimitives.description: Horizontal dashed cut line across all four panels at height EXD from bottom

geometryPrimitives.label: Pull Tab Notch
geometryPrimitives.description: Small triangular or rectangular tab protruding from strip edge at seam position — consumer grips this to start tear

tear-strip.geometryBehavior: Two parallel horizontal lines span the entire perimeter of the box at heights EXD and EXD+strip_width. At the glue seam edge, the lines are angled at GFA degrees to allow clean separation through the glue area. The pull notch is a small protrusion from the strip at one corner of the front panel.
validationRules: Strip width (distance between perforations) >= 5mm
EXD > minimum bottom closure height (strip must not interfere with bottom mechanism)
Perforation lines must be continuous across all panels with no gaps at crease lines
At glue seam, GFA angle allows both surfaces to separate cleanly
tear-strip.3dFoldingNotes: Tear strip encircles the box. When consumer pulls the notch, the strip tears along both perforations simultaneously, separating the top portion of the box from the bottom like removing a lid.
tear-strip.artworkNotes: Artwork must account for tear strip position — do not place critical text or barcodes across the perforation lines. The tear strip itself may carry a 'tear here' instruction graphic.
productionRisks: Perforation must be precisely specified for the die — too little = hard to tear; too much = accidental tear in transit
GFA angle at glue seam is critical — wrong angle = strip does not separate cleanly at seam

centered-divider.label: Centered Internal Divider
centered-divider.description: A panel that folds inward from one side panel and extends across the interior of the box parallel to the front/back faces, dividing the interior into two equal compartments. The divider is attached by a structural crease to the interior face of one side panel. Its free edge contains a slot or folded tongue that locks into the opposite side panel. Height of divider = H (full interior height). Depth of divider = L (spans the full length between front and back panels). In the flat dieline, the divider appears as an extension panel attached to one side panel. Parameters: OD1/OD2 (slot dimensions on divider), DL (divider lock tab length).
centered-divider.role: Divides interior into 2 equal compartments for dual-product packaging

inputs.name: DL
inputs.label: Divider Lock Tab Length
inputs.description: Length of the tab/slot at free end of divider that locks it to opposite side panel

faces.label: Centered Divider Panel
faces.note: The divider panel must be slightly narrower than L to account for material thickness at folds

structuralCreases.label: Divider Hinge
structuralCreases.description: Vertical crease attaching divider to side panel interior face. Divider folds 90° inward.

geometryPrimitives.label: Divider Lock Slot
geometryPrimitives.description: Slot in opposite side panel (side-B interior face) that receives the divider free edge tab/lock

centered-divider.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline, the divider panel appears attached to one side panel (between the side panel and the glue tab). It folds 90° inward when box is erected. Its free edge (width = DL) folds and inserts into a slot on the opposite side panel interior.
validationRules: Divider height must = H
Divider width must = L - 2T to account for material at both front and back panels
Divider lock slot position on opposite side panel must be exactly L - T from hinge side
Divider must not conflict with bottom closure mechanism geometry
centered-divider.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Erect box body. (2) Fold divider 90° inward from side-A. (3) Insert divider free edge tab into slot on side-B interior. Divider is now fixed. Load two products (one per compartment). (4) Close bottom and top closures.
centered-divider.artworkNotes: Divider face may be printed — visible through box window or when top is open. Consider printing on divider face for dual-product differentiation.
productionRisks: Divider width calculation must account for material thickness — failure to do so causes buckle or gap
Lock tab/slot system requires precise die — tolerance sensitive

integrated-partition.label: Integrated Partitions (6-Cell Grid)
integrated-partition.description: Two perpendicular divider panels attached to opposite body panels that interlock at their crossing point to create a grid of 6 cells (2 columns × 3 rows — or equivalent based on PD1/PD2). Each partition attaches to one body panel by a structural crease. They slot together at the center cross-point via matching half-depth slots (one slotted from top, one from bottom). After interlocking, the two panels stand perpendicular inside the box creating 6 equal compartments. Parameters: PD1 (partition depth 1), PD2 (partition depth 2).
integrated-partition.role: Creates 6 internal compartments for multi-product packaging (e.g., cosmetics, vials)

inputs.name: PD1
inputs.label: Partition Depth 1
inputs.description: Depth of the first partition panel (parallel to W)

inputs.name: PD2
inputs.label: Partition Depth 2
inputs.description: Depth of the second partition panel (parallel to L)

geometryPrimitives.label: Interlocking Cross Slots
geometryPrimitives.description: Each partition has a slot at its center running from one edge inward to H/2. When partitions are crossed and slots engaged, they lock perpendicular.

integrated-partition.geometryBehavior: Both partitions appear in the flat dieline attached to their respective body panels. Partition 1 extends from front panel bottom edge. Partition 2 extends from back panel bottom edge. When folded in during assembly they cross at 90° and the interlocking slots fix them perpendicular. This creates a 2×3 = 6 cell grid (3 rows across L, 2 columns across W — or vice versa depending on which panels partitions attach to).
validationRules: PD1 + PD2 <= W - 2T (partitions must fit across box width)
Partition height = H
Cross slots must be at exactly H/2 depth, width = T + clearance
Partitions must not conflict with auto-lock/snap-lock bottom geometry
integrated-partition.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Erect box. (2) Fold partition 1 inward from front panel. (3) Fold partition 2 inward from back panel. (4) Push partition 2 slot over partition 1 tab at crossing point. They lock perpendicular. (5) Load products. (6) Close top and bottom.
integrated-partition.artworkNotes: Partition faces are interior — typically not printed unless product showcase or scent/product differentiation is needed.
productionRisks: Cross-slot tolerance is critical — too tight = won't assemble; too loose = partitions collapse
Material thickness must be accounted for in partition width

built-in-insert.label: Built-in Product Insert
built-in-insert.description: Flap panels extending inward from the top and/or bottom edges of the side panels to grip and cradle the product at specific heights inside the box. The insert panels fold in before product loading, creating a platform or cradle that holds the product centered and prevents it from shifting during transport. Described by multiple dimensions D1–D6 (insert dimensions for each fold of each insert panel), TFW (tuck flap width), DFR (dust flap radius), DFW (dust flap width), GFW (glue flap width). Two inserts per side panel end = 4 total inserts in a full implementation.
built-in-insert.role: Internal product cradle, prevents movement during transit — ideal for fragile items
requiredAnchors: top and bottom side panel edges
built-in-insert.geometryBehavior: Each insert panel is a multi-fold assembly: multiple parallel creases divide the panel into sub-sections that fold in a Z or S pattern, creating a layered shelf or cradle at a specific depth inside the box. The D1–D6 dimensions specify the widths of each fold segment.
validationRules: Total insert depth (sum of alternating D segments) must = W (spans full interior width when folded)
Insert must not conflict with tuck flap or dust flap when closed
D segments must account for material thickness at each fold
built-in-insert.3dFoldingNotes: Insert panels fold in a zigzag (accordion) pattern. The final folded form creates a shelf surface inside the box at a controlled height. Product rests on this shelf. Top and bottom inserts grip the product from both ends.
built-in-insert.artworkNotes: Insert panels are interior — not typically printed. May receive product identification text for packing line use.
productionRisks: Multiple folds in insert = paper weakening at each crease — use 1.5× standard caliper or reinforced board
Incorrect D dimensions = insert does not reach opposite wall and fails to support product

product-mount.label: Product Mount Structure
product-mount.description: An internal cradle structure formed by extending the side wall panels inward through angled cuts and fold-in tab sections. Two opposing side panel extensions fold inward and interlock to create a horizontal shelf or cradle at a specific height inside the box. The mount holds the product in a fixed position — particularly valuable for electronics, tools, or fragile devices that must not shift in transit. The mount is formed by 'tucking' the extended portion of two side walls (one from each side panel) inward: each extension is die-cut with a specific depth (D1, D2) and has a slot/tab that interlocks with the opposite extension, creating a rigid platform inside. Parameters: D1 (first mount flap depth from side panel edge inward), D2 (second mount flap depth), SR (slot radius at interlock), TL (tab length), TR (tab radius), TD1 (tab depth 1), TD2 (tab depth 2), PR (punch radius at slot ends).
product-mount.role: Fixes product in position inside box — prevents movement and absorbs shock from bumpy transport

inputs.name: D1
inputs.label: Mount Depth 1
inputs.description: Depth of first mount tab (from sideA interior edge inward toward box center)

inputs.name: D2
inputs.label: Mount Depth 2
inputs.description: Depth of second mount tab (from sideB interior edge inward toward box center)

inputs.name: SR
inputs.label: Slot Radius
inputs.description: Radius of the rounded slot end used for interlocking the two mount tabs

faces.label: Mount Tab from Side-A
faces.note: Folds inward from top edge of side-A panel at defined height, creating shelf surface

faces.label: Mount Tab from Side-B
faces.note: Folds inward from top edge of side-B panel at defined height, interlocks with mount-tab-sideA

geometryPrimitives.label: Mount Interlock Slot on Tab A
geometryPrimitives.description: Slot cut into free edge of mount-tab-sideA, receives the tab of mount-tab-sideB

geometryPrimitives.label: Mount Interlock Slot on Tab B
geometryPrimitives.description: Slot cut into free edge of mount-tab-sideB, receives the tab of mount-tab-sideA

geometryPrimitives.label: Locking Tab Profile
geometryPrimitives.description: Tongue shape on each mount tab that inserts into the opposite slot

anchors.position: horizontal score line on sideA at D1 from top of panel
horizontal score line on sideB at D2 from top of panel

product-mount.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline the mount tabs appear as rectangular extensions above the side panel body zones (in the same area as top dust flaps but deeper). Each tab has a cut slot and tongue. D1 + D2 = approximately W (the two tabs together span the interior width when folded). The interlock point is at approximately W/2 inside the box.
validationRules: D1 + D2 must be approximately equal to W (both tabs together span full interior width)
Mount hinge height must not conflict with body panel creases
Mount tab must not overlap with top closure geometry
Slot width = tongue width + 1mm clearance
product-mount.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Erect box body. (2) Fold mount tab from side-A inward 90°. (3) Fold mount tab from side-B inward 90°. (4) Interlock the two tab tongues into each other's slots. (5) A rigid horizontal shelf is now fixed at the defined height. (6) Place product on shelf. (7) Close top and bottom closures normally.
product-mount.artworkNotes: Mount tab exterior faces are visible through the side openings before top closure is applied. May carry product identification marks for assembly line use.
productionRisks: Mount geometry is highly size-dependent — D1+D2 must exactly equal W minus material tolerance
Slot-tongue interlock must be verified with paper prototype before full production run

reversible-lid-panel.label: Reversible Lid Panel
reversible-lid-panel.description: The reversible lid is the top closure panel in a skillet or crash-bottom box where the lid can be flipped open without fully detaching. The lid panel is attached to the back panel top edge by a structural crease. When the box is closed, the lid panel folds downward over the front face and is locked by an inner tab panel that inserts into a slot on the front panel. To open: the user pushes the lid backward (rotating 180°) so it stands upright or leans against the back, revealing the full opening. The inner tab is a small panel attached to the lid interior face that locks into insert slots (SL1/SL2) on the box. Parameters for skillet variant: DFW (dust flap width), OD1–OD4 (outer dimensional offsets), SL1 (slot 1 length), SL2 (slot 2 length), SW2 (slot 2 width), SR2 (slot 2 radius), EA1 (end angle 1 in degrees), EA2 (end angle 2 in degrees).
reversible-lid-panel.role: Top access lid that rotates 180° to open — provides quick, clean access without detaching

inputs.name: OD1
inputs.label: Outer Offset Dimension 1
inputs.description: Controls lid panel width offset

inputs.name: EA1
inputs.label: End Angle 1
inputs.description: Angle of lid panel end cut, creates the skillet-style angled end closure

faces.label: Reversible Lid Panel
faces.note: Lid panel height equals box H — covers entire front face when closed

faces.label: Inner Lock Tab Panel
faces.note: Small panel attached to interior of lid, folds inward to engage slots

structuralCreases.label: Lid-to-Back-Panel Hinge
structuralCreases.description: The primary hinge crease allowing 180° rotation

structuralCreases.label: Inner Tab Hinge
structuralCreases.description: Crease attaching inner lock tab to lid face interior

geometryPrimitives.label: Insert Slot 1
geometryPrimitives.description: Slot on box body into which the inner tab inserts when lid is closed

geometryPrimitives.label: Insert Slot 2
geometryPrimitives.description: Second slot for additional locking engagement

reversible-lid-panel.geometryBehavior: The lid panel appears in the flat dieline as a large panel attached to the back panel top edge, extending upward in the dieline. It is typically as wide as the front panel (L) and as tall as H. The inner tab is a small extension attached to the lid face that folds 90° inward when the lid is closed. The angled ends (EA1, EA2) create the characteristic skillet-end profile.
validationRules: Lid height must equal H so it covers the full front face
Inner tab must reach and engage insert slot when lid is in closed position
SL1 width must match inner tab tongue width + 1mm clearance
EA1 and EA2 angles create the skillet end profile — must be symmetric unless intentionally asymmetric
reversible-lid-panel.3dFoldingNotes: 3D behavior: When lid is closed — the back panel hinge allows the lid to rotate forward 180° and come to rest flat against the front face. The inner tab engages the insert slots on the front panel, locking the lid. To open: press sides of lid slightly inward to disengage inner tab from slots, then rotate lid backward 180° — it either stands vertical against the back panel or is held by a secondary stop. This gives quick one-hand access.
reversible-lid-panel.artworkNotes: The exterior of the lid (which covers the front face when closed) is the primary display surface — key branding real estate. Both front-when-closed and open-back positions should be considered in artwork.
productionRisks: Inner tab slot engagement must be calibrated to close firmly but open easily — tolerance-critical
Angled end geometry (EA1, EA2) requires precise die matching for skillet profile

gusset-roof-panel.label: Gusset Roof Panel Assembly
gusset-roof-panel.description: The gusset roof is an angled top closure that forms a tent or house-roof shape over the box. Instead of a flat top, the box has two slanted roof panels meeting at a ridge, with triangular gusset panels at each end filling the corner gaps. This creates a visually premium appearance and provides extra structural rigidity. The bottom of the gusset roof is a crash/auto-lock bottom. Parameters: BFW (bottom flap width), TFW (top flap width for the angled ridge closure), OD (outer diameter of tear hole if combined with tear strip), GFW (glue flap width). The roof angle is determined by the ratio of the ridge height to the box width W.
gusset-roof-panel.role: Decorative angled tent-roof top providing premium appearance and structural rigidity

inputs.name: BFW
inputs.label: Bottom Flap Width
inputs.description: Width of the bottom closure flap on the gusset roof variant

inputs.name: TFW
inputs.label: Top Ridge Flap Width
inputs.description: The ridge closing flap that joins the two angled roof panels at the apex

faces.label: Gusset Roof Front Slope
faces.description: Angled panel attached to front panel top edge, slopes upward toward the ridge

faces.label: Gusset Roof Back Slope
faces.description: Matching angled panel attached to back panel top edge

faces.label: Gusset Triangle Side-A
faces.description: Triangular fill panel attached to side-A top edge, fills the corner gap between the two sloped panels

faces.label: Gusset Triangle Side-B
faces.description: Triangular fill panel attached to side-B top edge

faces.label: Ridge Closure Flap
faces.description: Small flap at the ridge apex that seals the top joint — width TFW

structuralCreases.description: The triangular gusset has an internal diagonal crease that allows it to fold in two planes simultaneously

gusset-roof-panel.geometryBehavior: In the flat dieline the gusset roof panels appear above the body H zone. The front and back slope panels are parallelograms (not rectangles) due to the angled roof geometry. The triangular side gussets are triangles with an internal diagonal crease. Roof angle = arctan(ridge_height / (W/2)). Ridge height determines the aesthetic steepness of the roof.
validationRules: Triangular gusset dimensions must be calculated from roof angle and W — cannot be arbitrary
Ridge closure flap TFW must be sufficient to glue or tuck the two slope panels together
All gusset panels must meet cleanly at the roof ridge — gap or overlap not permitted
gusset-roof-panel.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly (extremely complex fold sequence): (1) Fold front slope panel upward to roof angle. (2) Fold back slope panel upward to matching angle. (3) Simultaneously fold the triangular gussets inward — each gusset folds on its internal diagonal crease to fill the angled corner. (4) Apply ridge closure flap to seal the apex. All four movements are interdependent — this box cannot be assembled in simple sequential steps like a standard carton. It is typically assembled by machine.
gusset-roof-panel.artworkNotes: Gusset roof creates strong visual presence. The two sloped faces and four visible gusset triangles all carry artwork. Layout requires careful 3D visualization. The ridge line is a sharp prominent design element.
productionRisks: Gusset geometry calculations are complex — requires professional packaging engineer
Triangular gusset crease position is critical — 1mm error causes gap or overlap at ridge
Box typically requires machine assembly — not suitable for hand-assembly at scale
Prototype mandatory before die creation

gusset-cover-panel.label: Gusset Tuck Cover Panel
gusset-cover-panel.description: A tuck-end cover where the four corners are reinforced by triangular gusset panels that fold inward with the tuck flap. Unlike a standard tuck flap (which is a simple rectangle), the gusset cover has folded triangular extensions at each corner. When the cover closes, the gussets fold inward to fill the side gaps (replacing the standard dust flaps) and provide extra corner rigidity. This significantly enhances structural integrity during handling. Parameters: TFW (tuck flap width), FW (front flap width for the tuck panel), GFW (glue flap width), FR (gusset fold radius — radius of the corner transition).
gusset-cover-panel.role: Reinforced corner tuck cover with integrated gusset panels replacing dust flaps

inputs.name: FR
inputs.label: Gusset Corner Fold Radius
inputs.description: The radius of the diagonal fold line at each corner of the gusset cover — controls how tightly the corner folds

faces.label: Left Gusset Side Panel
faces.description: Extends from main cover left edge — folds inward to reinforce left corner

structuralCreases.description: 45-degree score from main cover corner to gusset triangle tip — allows triangular gusset to fold inward

gusset-cover-panel.geometryBehavior: The gusset cover panel appears in the flat dieline as a larger, more complex shape than a standard tuck flap. It has trapezoidal or extended side wings at each corner with diagonal crease lines. When closed, the diagonal creases activate: the corner triangles fold inward under the main cover, creating reinforced corners. The main cover panel then tucks into the box.
validationRules: Diagonal crease angle must be exactly 45° from panel corner
Gusset side extensions must equal W in unfolded width (they span the side openings)
TFW must be sufficient for secure tuck even after gusset material folds
gusset-cover-panel.3dFoldingNotes: Assembly: (1) Fold gusset side panels inward 90° simultaneously. (2) Press diagonal crease lines — the corner triangles fold inward and fill the gap between the side panels and the main box opening. (3) Fold and tuck the main cover down into the box. The gussets are now folded inside, creating reinforced interior corners.
gusset-cover-panel.artworkNotes: Gusset cover exterior is fully visible — design must accommodate the wider shape in flat artwork. The diagonal crease lines create subtle shadow lines on the closed box top.
productionRisks: Diagonal crease positions must be precise — error creates visible gap at corners
Gusset covers are typically assembled by machine — hand assembly is slow

skillet-insert-panel.label: Skillet Insert Panel (Separated Two-Piece)
skillet-insert-panel.description: In the separated (two-piece) skillet box, the box body and lid are two completely separate dieline pieces. The main body is an open-top tray/sleeve, and the lid is a reversible cover that slides or flips over it. The insert panel is a flat shelf attached to the inner front wall of the main body, forming a platform that holds the product in position. Parameters (from separated-skillet-box): FL (front length), BL (back length), TFW (tuck flap width), GD (gap dimension), OD (outer diameter of snap hole), SR (slot radius), SL (slot length), SW1 (slot width 1), SW2 (slot width 2).
skillet-insert-panel.role: Inner product-holding shelf in separated two-piece skillet box
skillet-insert-panel.geometryBehavior: The insert panel appears in the flat dieline as an extension of the front wall of the skillet base. It folds 90° inward to create a horizontal shelf parallel to the box base. The shelf is separated from the base by gap GD.
validationRules: Insert width must = L - 2T
Insert height must = W - GD
Snap slot must maintain margin from all edges
skillet-insert-panel.3dFoldingNotes: The insert folds inward from the front wall after the skillet body is assembled. The lid then slides or flips over the body with the insert holding the product centered.
skillet-insert-panel.artworkNotes: Insert is interior — not typically printed.
productionRisks: Two separate pieces (body + lid) require two separate dielines and must be matched in production

templatePartMatrix.description: Maps each template to its required and optional reusable parts. This matrix drives implementation priorities — parts used by many templates should be built first.

templateDetails.templateName: Reverse Tuck End Folding Carton Box
templateDetails.shortDescription: Classic four-panel folding carton with tuck closures on top and bottom that insert from opposite sides (front vs back).
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, electronics accessories, general retail products. The most widely used folding carton style globally.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The reverse tuck end allows both top and bottom to be closed from opposite sides, which means the box can be filled from either end on automated packaging lines. The opposing directions create natural resistance to accidental opening — each closure locks against the pressure that would open the other. Extremely paper-efficient: no glue needed at closures, just die-cut tongue-and-dust-flap mechanism.
topClosureParts: reverse-tuck-flap (attached to back panel top edge)
bottomClosureParts: reverse-tuck-flap (attached to front panel bottom edge — inserts from back direction)

sizeFlaps: TFW — Tuck Flap Width (depth of tuck insertion)
TFR — Tuck Flap Radius (corner rounding of tuck leading edge)

templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Most common carton style. All parts are basic rectangles plus simple radius cut. Building this first validates the entire body-strip + dust-flap + tuck-flap pipeline.

topClosure.description: Reverse tuck flap attached to TOP of BACK panel. Inserts into box opening from the front face direction. Width = L, insertion depth = TFW. Leading edge has TFR radius at each corner and two small triangular lock notches.
foldRelationships: dust-flap-topA folds 90° inward from top of side-A BEFORE tuck flap
dust-flap-topB folds 90° inward from top of side-B BEFORE tuck flap
tuck-flap folds 90° then inserts into opening OVER the dust flaps
geometryNotes: Tuck flap width L must match box front opening exactly
TFR corner radius prevents paper split at sharp corners during insertion
Lock notches at x = DFW from each side catch on inside of dust flap edge

bottomClosure.description: Reverse tuck flap attached to BOTTOM of FRONT panel. Inserts into box opening from the back face direction (opposite to top). Width = L, insertion depth = TFW.
foldRelationships: same as top closure but attached to front panel bottom, inserts from opposite direction
geometryNotes: Bottom tuck flap is identical to top — same parameters TFW, TFR, DFW

reliefOrNotches: corner-relief-notch at junction of body panel crease and dust flap hinge — small semicircle approx radius 2mm prevents paper tearing at fold intersection
scoreLines: 4 vertical body creases at x = W, W+L, W+L+W, W+L+W+L
4 top horizontal hinges for tuck flap and both dust flaps
glueZones: glue-tab full height rectangle — hatched in dieline

unknownParameters: exact lock notch dimensions (not exposed in CefBox UI — standard industry value ~2mm protrusion)

expectedGraphContract.faceTreeNotes: Root = panel-front. Children: side-A (crease W from left), back via side-A (crease W+L), side-B via back (crease 2W+L), glue-tab via side-B (crease 2W+2L). Top tuck attaches to top-back. Bottom tuck attaches to bottom-front. All dust flaps attach to their side panel top/bottom edges.

hardParts: lock notch exact position must align with DFW — requires runtime calculation
knownRisks: DFW exactly W/2 = dust flap collision — enforce W/2 - 2mm

templateDetails.templateName: Straight Tuck End Folding Carton Box
templateDetails.shortDescription: Four-panel folding carton where both top and bottom tuck flaps insert from the same side of the box.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Products inserted from a consistent direction on automated lines. Common for cosmetics, medical devices, food supplements.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: When both ends of a box are opened from the same side, the product can be inserted or removed from either end without flipping the box.
