On automated assembly lines where product always enters from the same direction, straight tuck simplifies robotics. The top and bottom closures both resist the same pulling direction, which can provide extra security on one side.
topClosureParts: straight-tuck-flap (top, attached to back panel top)
bottomClosureParts: straight-tuck-flap (bottom, attached to back panel bottom — same direction as top)
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Essentially identical to reverseTuckEnd — only the panel attachment changes. Reuses all same parts.

topClosure.description: Tuck flap attached to TOP of BACK panel — same as reverse tuck top.
foldRelationships: identical to reverseTuckEnd top closure
geometryNotes: Geometry identical to reverse tuck flap — same parameters

bottomClosure.description: Tuck flap attached to BOTTOM of BACK panel — enters from the same back face direction as top closure. KEY DIFFERENCE from reverse tuck: both on back panel.
foldRelationships: bottom tuck also attached to back panel bottom edge — inserts from back direction like the top
geometryNotes: Bottom tuck inserts from SAME direction as top (both from back) — opposite to reverse tuck

knownRisks: Configuration flag needed: top_attachment = back, bottom_attachment = back (vs reverse: top=back, bottom=front)
recommendedBuildOrder: implement as variant of reverseTuckEnd with attachment-side parameter

templateDetails.templateName: Auto Lock Bottom Folding Carton Box
templateDetails.shortDescription: Tuck top (reverse tuck) with auto-lock (crash-lock) bottom that snaps open automatically when box is erected.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Heavier products, retail packaging, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals. Ideal for automated box erection lines.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The auto-lock bottom eliminates the manual step of closing the box bottom. On high-speed packing lines, boxes must be erected in milliseconds — the auto-lock bottom springs open automatically when the flat box is pushed open, saving assembly time. The bottom is also stronger than a tuck flap because the interlocking mechanism distributes load across four panels. Uses a reverse tuck top for easy consumer access.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Very commonly used style. Auto-lock bottom geometry is complex but unlocks 10+ templates when implemented. Critical P1 after basic tuck variants.

topClosure.description: Standard reverse tuck flap on back panel top edge — same as reverseTuckEnd.
foldRelationships: dust flaps fold in, then tuck flap inserts

bottomClosure.description: Auto-lock crash bottom: four pre-glued panels that snap into a locked rectangle when box is pushed open. Two major flaps (front, back) with diagonal scores. Two minor flaps (side-A, side-B). One additional auto-lock glue panel attached to one major flap edge. Factory pre-glues the assembly while flat.
foldRelationships: All four bottom flaps fold outward 90° during erection
Diagonal scores on major flaps activate during the flattening/erecting motion
Glue panel (attached to front major flap) is pre-glued to back major flap interior
geometryNotes: Major flap height = W/2 + ~5mm overlap
Minor flap height = W/2 - ~2mm (must not overlap minor flaps from opposite sides)
Diagonal score starts at approximately (W/4, 0) from the corner and runs to (0, W/2) — angle = arctan(W/2 / (W/4)) = arctan(2) ≈ 63.4°
Exact diagonal position varies by box proportions — must be calculated

scoreLines: horizontal hinges for top tuck + dust flaps
horizontal hinges for all 4 auto-lock bottom flaps
diagonal score lines on 2 major bottom flaps (4 diagonal lines total)
glueZones: auto-lock pre-glue zone on glue panel

unknownParameters: exact diagonal crease start/end coordinates (function of W and L — must be engineered)
exact major flap overlap amount beyond W/2

knownRisks: Diagonal crease angle is the most critical calculation in this template — wrong value = bottom fails to erect or collapse

templateDetails.templateName: Snap Lock Bottom Folding Carton Box
templateDetails.shortDescription: Tuck top with manually assembled snap-lock bottom. Bottom uses interlocking tongue-in-slot mechanism — no adhesive needed.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Slightly heavier products, short-to-medium runs, situations where auto-lock tooling is not available.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The snap-lock bottom provides a strong base without factory pre-gluing (which requires specialized machinery). A consumer or packer manually folds in the side flaps, then snaps the tongue of one major flap into the slot of the other. This works well for smaller brands or situations where the auto-lock machine is not economically justified. The snap mechanism resists accidental opening better than a simple tuck bottom.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Used by 12+ templates. Snap-lock bottom is the foundation of the most feature-rich templates.

topClosure.description: Standard reverse tuck flap — identical to reverseTuckEnd.

bottomClosure.description: Snap-lock: front major flap has tongue, back major flap has slot. Two side minor flaps fold in first. Then back (slot) folds in. Then front (tongue) folds in and tongue snaps through slot.
foldRelationships: snap-minor-sideA folds 90° inward first
snap-minor-sideB folds 90° inward first
snap-major-B (slot carrier) folds 90° inward second
snap-major-A (tongue carrier) folds 90° inward last — tongue bends and snaps through slot in B
geometryNotes: Tongue shape: rectangular with rounded corners, width approximately L/4 to L/3, depth ~6mm
Slot in major-B: width = tongue width + 1mm clearance, length = tongue depth + 1mm
Slot is positioned at center of major-B, approximately 5–8mm from fold hinge edge

unknownParameters: exact tongue width, depth, and slot position — CefBox doesn't expose these; they are calculated from L and W

hardParts: tongue shape and slot dimensions — tolerances are critical
knownRisks: Tongue too wide = hard manual assembly
Slot too wide = bottom opens under load
recommendedBuildOrder: snap-lock-bottom-panel — build tongue/slot as configurable sub-component

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton Gift Box with Folded Handle
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom box with an integrated multi-panel folded carry handle on top. Handle doubles as the top closure (catalog lock type). Optional windows available.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Gift packaging, chocolates, confectioneries, seasonal collections, clothing gift boxes. Any product that benefits from an integrated carry handle.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Providing a carry handle on the box itself eliminates the need for a separate bag or handle attachment. The folded handle is created entirely from the carton board — no adhesive, string, or separate components. The catalog lock top simultaneously seals the box and completes the handle structure. Auto-lock bottom provides a strong base for heavier gift products.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Complex folded handle requires careful engineering. Low volume template but high brand value. Depends on auto-lock bottom (P1).

topClosure.description: Folded handle assembly replaces the standard tuck flap. Handle panels extend from the top of both front and back panels. The handle incorporates a catalog lock (tab-in-slot) mechanism that seals the box top while holding the handle arch in position. Consumer lifts by gripping the bridge panel through the finger slot.
parts: folded-handle (front shoulder + back shoulder + bridge + palm pad)
foldRelationships: Front shoulder folds 90° upward from front panel top edge
Back shoulder folds 90° upward from back panel top edge
Bridge panel folds perpendicular connecting front and back shoulders
Palm pad folds 180° onto bridge (double-layer for comfort)
Catalog lock tab inserts through slot in front or back panel to secure assembly
geometryNotes: HL = clear finger slot width — minimum 40mm for adult hand
HT = height of handle arch above box top — minimum 15mm
SR = finger slot corner radius — minimum 8mm to prevent paper cuts
SD1/SD2 = shoulder depths (height of the two vertical side walls of the handle)
FW1/FW2 = flap widths that lock the handle down to the box top
OD = optional circular hole in palm pad for additional grip feature

bottomClosure.description: Auto-lock crash bottom — identical to autoLockBottom template.
foldRelationships: auto-erect when box tube is pushed open

unknownParameters: exact 3D fold sequence for handle assembly
precise geometry of catalog lock engagement within handle structure

knownRisks: Handle must bear product weight — verify board caliper

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton Box with Circular Hang Hole
templateDetails.shortDescription: Standard folding carton with a rectangular panel extension above the top tuck flap, containing a punched circular hole for retail peg-hook display.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Retail display products: cosmetics, electronics accessories, confectioneries, small household items. Designed to hang on euro-hook or standard peg hook displays.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Retail stores use peg hook displays for space efficiency. The hang hole panel extension allows the same box structure to be displayed hanging (on pegs) rather than standing on a shelf. The circular hole is double-layered (tuck flap + extension glued together) for strength under product weight. The snap-lock bottom provides reliable bottom strength for heavier retail items.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Hang hole is simple geometry. Depends on snap-lock bottom (P1). Very common retail template.

topClosure.description: Extended tuck flap assembly. The tuck flap has an additional rectangular hang panel above it (height HL). The entire assembly (hang panel + tuck flap) is attached to the back panel top edge. The circular hole (diameter OD) is punched through the center of the hang panel at position (L/2, HL/2).
foldRelationships: The hang panel extension is continuous above the tuck flap — they are one connected panel with a fold crease separating them
When closed: tuck flap folds down into box, hang panel protrudes above box top
In assembled box, both layers (front extension + hang panel) are glued for double-layer strength
geometryNotes: HL = height of hang panel extension above tuck flap fold line
HW = width of hang panel = L (full width)
OD = diameter of circular hole — typically 6mm (euro) or 8mm (US standard)
SR = slot radius if euro-slot variant used instead of circle

bottomClosure.description: Snap-lock bottom — same as snapLockBottom template.

hardParts: double-layer hang panel requires instruction in assembly guide
hole must be die-punched through both layers simultaneously
recommendedBuildOrder: build after snap-lock bottom is working
add circular-hang-hole as geometry-only feature on hang extension face

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton Box with Hang Tab
templateDetails.shortDescription: Folding carton with a folded double-layer hang tab attached to the tuck flap top edge, containing a euro-slot for peg display. Different from hang hole: the tab folds out from the tuck flap rather than being a flat panel extension.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Retail display: cosmetics, electronics, toys, confectioneries. The folded tab is more durable and provides better load distribution than a simple punch hole.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The folded hang tab creates a stronger, double-thickness hanging structure compared to a single-layer punch hole. The euro-slot shape provides a larger engagement area on the peg hook than a simple circle. The tab folds 180° onto itself and is glued, creating a stiff, strong tab. This design is used when higher product weights or more premium presentation is required.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Folded hang tab geometry is more complex than circular hole. Medium priority — depends on snap-lock bottom.

topClosure.description: Tuck flap with hang tab extension above. The hang tab is a narrow rectangle (width TW) centered on the tuck flap, extending above it by height SAL*2. It has a fold crease at midpoint. The euro-slot is cut through the upper half. After assembly, the outer half folds 180° and is glued to inner half — double layer.
foldRelationships: Outer half of hang tab folds 180° back onto inner half at the midpoint crease
Both halves are glued together in factory
Euro-slot punched through both layers
geometryNotes: TW = tab body width (not full panel width — tab is narrower than tuck flap)
SAL = total tab height / 2 = half-length of each tab panel
SL = slot length (euro-slot elongated dimension)
SW = slot width (euro-slot narrow dimension)
FR = fillet radius at slot ends (creates the euro-slot capsule shape)

unknownParameters: exact fold and glue sequence for tab double-layer

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton Box with Locking Tab on Top and Bottom
templateDetails.shortDescription: Folding carton with catalog-lock (tab-in-slot) closures on BOTH top AND bottom. Resists accidental opening from both ends.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Products requiring tamper resistance without a tear strip. Electronics, cosmetics, gift sets where the consumer expects to work to open the box.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Standard tuck flaps are easy to open — the tab just slides out. The locking tab (catalog lock) requires the user to push the tab through a slot, which requires deliberate action. Applying this to both top and bottom means neither end can be accidentally opened. Common in products where contents must stay secure during shipping and retail display.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Locking lip flap is used in 7+ templates. Building it unlocks many complex templates.

topClosure.description: Locking lip flap on top (attached to front panel top edge). Contains a tab of length TL that projects down and inserts through a slot cut in the back panel at the top edge. The slot has rounded ends (radius PR). When closed: flap covers box top, tab is locked inside.
foldRelationships: dust flaps in first
locking flap folds down last, tab pushes through slot
geometryNotes: TL = tab horizontal length (centered on flap)
TD1 = primary depth of tab insertion
TD2 = secondary step (if tab has stepped profile)
TR = tab corner radius
PR = punch radius at slot ends

bottomClosure.description: Also locking lip flap on bottom (attached to back panel bottom edge — matching slot cut in front panel bottom zone). Identical geometry to top locking flap.
geometryNotes: Both top and bottom use same TL/TD1/TD2/PR parameters

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Box with Built-in Inserts
templateDetails.shortDescription: Reverse tuck end box with accordion-folded insert panels integrated into the side walls. Inserts grip the product from top and bottom to prevent movement in transit.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Fragile products: glass jars, cosmetic tubes, electronic components, medical devices. Any product that must not shift during shipping.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Standard foam inserts or separate cardboard inserts add cost and waste. Built-in inserts are formed from the same carton board as the box itself — no extra components needed. The accordion-fold panels create a spring-like grip that conforms slightly to the product shape. Particularly valuable for fragile cosmetic packaging (glass tubs, serums) that need cushioning but cannot use foam.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Built-in inserts are unique to this template. Complex multi-fold accordion geometry.

internalStructures.name: Built-in Inserts (4 total)
internalStructures.description: Two insert assemblies per side panel (top and bottom), creating a total of 4 accordion panels. Each insert is a multi-fold strip attached to the side panel top/bottom edge. D1–D6 are the widths of each fold sub-section. When the inserts fold inward (during assembly after box erection), they create a Z/S-shaped shelf inside the box at both the top and bottom ends, gripping the product.
internalStructures.foldSequence: Each insert has 3–6 parallel creases. Folds alternate direction (valley, mountain, valley...) creating accordion. Final position: the insert panel floats inside the box, spring-loaded against the product.

unknownParameters: exact fold direction of each D segment (valley vs mountain)
total D1+D2+D3+D4+D5+D6 must equal W — constraint must be enforced

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton with Integrated Partitions
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom carton with two built-in perpendicular divider panels that interlock inside the box to create 6 equal compartments.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Multi-product packaging: 6-unit cosmetics sets, vial collections, spice jars, small bottles. Any 6-item set needing organized presentation.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Packaging 6 identical items in one box requires dividers to prevent items from clinking or scratching each other. Separate divider inserts add cost and assembly time. Integrated partitions are cut and folded from the same carton — they fold inward during box assembly and interlock at their center crossing point to create a rigid 6-cell grid. No glue needed for the partitions — they are mechanically locked.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Unique partition geometry. Depends on auto-lock bottom (P1). Used only by this template.

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton with Built-in Centered Divider
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom with slit-slot tuck top and a single centered divider panel that divides the interior into two equal compartments.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Twin-product packaging: paired cosmetics (day/night cream), matched accessories, two-flavor confectioneries, gift sets of two items.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: When selling two related products together, a divider creates a clean presentation and prevents the items from shifting or scratching each other. The centered divider is integrated into the box — no separate component. The slit-slot tuck top (tab closure) provides more secure closure than a plain tuck since the two compartments may make the box top feel less stable without it.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Centered divider is reused in 3 templates. Worth implementing after locking-lip-flap is done.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap Lock Bottom Carton with Divider and Windows
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom carton with a tab-closure top, centered divider, and three window cutouts (one on each side panel and one on the front). Most complex standard template.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Twin products with display windows — perfumes, paired cosmetics, gift sets where both the packaging and products are part of the visual presentation.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Combining a divider with window cutouts creates a premium presentation for twin-product packaging. The windows allow consumers to see both products simultaneously from multiple angles (three-sided visibility). The tab closure is used instead of a plain tuck because the divider adds internal structure that makes a simple tuck less stable — the tab ensures the top stays firmly closed.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Most parameter-rich standard template. Depends on locking-lip-flap, centered-divider, snap-lock-bottom, and window-cutout all being implemented first.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap Lock Bottom Folding Carton with Tab Closure
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom carton with catalog-lock (tab-in-slot) top closure. More secure top than plain tuck while maintaining the easy-erect snap bottom.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Heavier products needing secure top closure. Electronics, cosmetic sets, food supplements.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Combines the ease of snap-lock bottom assembly with the security of a locking tab top. Plain tuck tops can be accidentally opened if the box is dropped or jostled. The tab-closure top prevents this, making it suitable for retail shelf presentation where opening during handling would be embarrassing or wasteful.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Straightforward combination of two P1/P2 parts. High usage template.

templateDetails.templateName: Auto-Lock Bottom Folding Carton with Tab Closure
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock (crash-lock) bottom with a catalog-lock tab-in-slot top. Best of both: fast auto bottom, secure locking top.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: High-volume retail packaging where both assembly speed (auto bottom) and secure closure (locking top) are required. Cosmetics, electronics, personal care.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: On automated packing lines, auto-lock bottoms save significant time. Adding a locking tab top means the finished package is tamper-resistant without a separate seal. This is the go-to template for brands that fill on automated lines and need a secure retail presentation.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: High-value template. Reuses auto-lock bottom (P1) + locking-lip-flap (P2). Direct combination.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap-Lock Bottom Folding Carton with Centered Divider
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom with tab-closure top and centered divider creating two compartments. More secure version of carton-with-centered-divider.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Twin products with snap-lock base: paired cosmetics, gift sets. Used when auto-lock machinery is not available.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Same use case as carton-with-centered-divider but with snap-lock instead of auto-lock bottom. Offers a divider + locking top combination for manufacturers using snap-lock tooling.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap-Lock Carton with Arc Handle
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom box with an arc-shaped carry handle integrated into the front and back panels — handle is cut from the body panels themselves.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Electronic components, small appliances, gift boxes for slightly heavy items. Any product needing a carry handle that is too heavy for a tuck-top box without reinforcement.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The arc handle is simpler to manufacture than the folded handle — it is cut and scored directly from the body panel without additional separate panels. The arch cutout creates a grip opening, and the material above the arch crease folds outward to form the grip bar. The snap-lock bottom provides the base strength needed for heavier products. No glue needed for the handle — it is self-formed from the panel.

decomposition.handleDescription: Arc handle consists of: (1) Two matching arch cutouts on front and back panels, centered horizontally at mid-height. (2) A horizontal hinge crease at the base of each arch. (3) The grip bar (material between arch cutout and body panel top edge) folds outward 90° from front and back, then the two grip bars lean toward each other and lock at the top, forming an arch. HR = radius of arch. HT = arch opening height. SR = corner radius of arch cutout for comfort.

templateDetails.templateName: Centered Tuck End Folding Carton
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom with a distinctive angled/peaked tuck top closure. The top has a V-shaped or stepped angled profile instead of a flat edge.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Premium retail packaging where the top profile creates a distinctive shelf presence. Cosmetics, candles, specialty foods.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: A flat-top tuck flap is functional but visually plain. An angled top creates a characteristic silhouette that differentiates the product on shelf without additional cost. The centered peak draws attention upward and makes the box taller-feeling than its actual height.

templateDetails.templateName: Gusset Roof Folding Carton with Tear Strip
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom carton with an angled tent-roof top (gusset roof) and a perforated tear strip for tamper-evident opening. Premium presentation with easy access.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Premium food packaging, cereals, specialty products, high-end confectioneries. The gusset roof provides shelf presence; the tear strip provides tamper evidence.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The gusset roof shape is instantly recognizable as premium packaging (similar to Toblerone or cereal boxes). It creates a large printable surface on the two sloped faces. The tear strip allows consumers to open the box without damaging the decorative top — instead of tearing through the tuck closure, they pull the strip to open the side, preserving the roof shape for reuse or display.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Gusset roof is the most complex geometry in the folding box category. Expert level — must be last.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap-Lock Folding Carton with Built-in Mount
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom box with a tab-closure top and an internal product mount formed by interlocking extensions of the side panels.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Electronics, tools, devices, or products that must be displayed in a fixed position inside the box. The mount positions the product precisely.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Some products (phones, power tools, small devices) need to sit in a specific position inside the box for both presentation and protection. Instead of foam inserts or separate cardboard mounts, this box creates the mount from extensions of the side walls. The mount is a shelf that holds the product at a defined height, preventing downward movement and absorbing shock.

templateDetails.templateName: Tuck End Folding Carton (Slot Tuck)
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom box with a tuck-end cover that has a slot cutout in the body for the tuck to engage — similar to the centered-tuck variant but with a slot mechanism.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Retail cosmetics, candles, premium products wanting a tuck-end top aesthetic combined with a strong bottom.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The slot-tuck mechanism provides a clean top appearance (no visible dust flaps) while using a slot to hold the tuck flap securely. The slot engages the tuck flap edge to prevent it from springing open. Combined with snap-lock bottom, this provides both an attractive top and a reliable base.

templateDetails.templateName: Skillet Box with Reversible Lid
templateDetails.shortDescription: Skillet-style (landscape orientation) folding carton with a reversible top cover that flips 180° to open. Single-piece construction.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Cigarettes, gum, small cookies, candies, compact products. Automated packaging line compatible.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Skillet-end cartons are designed for automated high-speed packaging lines (similar to cigarette packaging). The landscape orientation and shallow height make them ideal for flat, compact products. The reversible lid provides one-hand access — no dust flaps to fold, no tabs to push. Just flip the lid open. The inner tab locks the lid closed when the user's not using it.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Skillet body + reversible lid = completely different architecture from standard folding cartons. Expert level.

templateDetails.templateName: Crash Bottom Folding Carton with Reversible Top Cover
templateDetails.shortDescription: Standard-body (portrait orientation) folding carton with crash-lock bottom and a reversible top cover. Pre-glued, flat-shipped, fast erection.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Chilled/frozen food, cereals, snacks, deli meats, cosmetics, gums, cigarettes. Any product where quick, convenient access is valued.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Extending the reversible lid concept from skillet to standard (taller) boxes allows the convenience of one-hand flip access for a wider range of products. The crash bottom provides fast, reliable base assembly. The pre-glued construction means the box arrives flat and can be erected in one push, making it ideal for high-speed filling operations.

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Carton with Gusset Cover and Crash Bottom
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock (crash-lock) bottom carton with a gusset tuck cover top that has reinforced corners. Premium structural integrity.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Wide range of products needing a premium top appearance. The gusset corners add visual interest and structural stiffness at corners.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Standard tuck flaps leave open corners at the top of the box — small triangular gaps where the dust flaps end and the tuck flap begins. The gusset cover fills these corners completely by incorporating triangular gusset panels that fold in with the main cover. This gives a cleaner, more finished look and increases corner rigidity. The crash bottom provides automated assembly.

templateDetails.templateName: Auto Lock Bottom Box with Full-Flap Bottom Panel
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom box where one major bottom flap is extended to cover the ENTIRE base, eliminating the center seam line visible on standard auto-lock bases.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Premium retail packaging: cosmetics, personal care, small electronics. Any product where a clean, uninterrupted base is important for presentation or barcode placement.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Standard auto-lock bottoms have a visible seam line down the center of the base where the two major flaps meet. For premium products this seam can look cheap. The full-flap variant extends one major flap to cover the entire base, creating a clean surface. It also distributes weight more evenly for slightly heavier products. The uninterrupted base provides maximum space for barcodes, lot codes, and regulatory text.

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Box with Circular Hang Hole and Window
templateDetails.shortDescription: Standard folding carton with both a hang hole (for peg display) and a window cutout (for product visibility). Designed for premium retail peg display.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Retail products needing both hanging display and product visibility: cosmetics, small electronics, packaged food, artisan products.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Combining hang hole and window gives the maximum retail impact: the product can be displayed on a peg hook (space-efficient, eye-level visibility) while consumers can see the product through the window (reducing purchase hesitation). This combination is standard for personal care and cosmetics products on pharmacy/beauty counter displays.

windowNotes.DR: Hang hole diameter (circular, similar to OD in with-circular-hang-hole)

templateDetails.templateName: Folding Box with Handle and Window
templateDetails.shortDescription: Folded-handle box with an additional window cutout on the front panel for product visibility. Auto-lock bottom.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Gift packaging with product showcase: chocolates, confectioneries, clothing. Combines carry convenience with visual display.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Adding a window to the handle box allows the product to be visible through the packaging while the carry handle makes it gift-ready. Perfect for chocolates or confectioneries where the consumer wants to see the product they're carrying as a gift.
templateDetails.reasonForPriority: Depends on folded-handle (P3) + window-cutout (P2). Most complex handle template.

templateDetails.templateName: Separated Skillet Box (Two-Piece)
templateDetails.shortDescription: Two separate dieline pieces: a skillet base (open-top sleeve/tray) and a reversible cover lid. The lid slides over the base or reverses open. An inner insert panel holds the product.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Cigarettes, gum, compact cookies, small electronics. Automated packaging lines requiring fast filling from the open top.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: The separated two-piece design allows the base and lid to be manufactured, printed, and assembled independently, providing greater flexibility in design and artwork. The reversible lid can be a different board stock, color, or treatment than the base. The inner insert panel in the base holds the product tightly in position.

templateDetails.templateName: Auto Lock Bottom Box with Tearable Strip Seal
templateDetails.shortDescription: Auto-lock bottom box with a perforated tear strip running around the box perimeter for tamper-evident consumer opening.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Food products, pharmaceuticals, any product requiring tamper evidence without a separate seal. Consumer tears the strip to open instead of lifting a tuck flap.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Some product categories require evidence that the package has not been opened before purchase. The tear strip creates a one-time tamper seal built into the box itself — no additional heat seal or sticker needed. Once the tear strip is removed, the box top becomes the reverse tuck closure. The auto-lock bottom provides fast automated base closure.

templateDetails.templateName: Snap Lock Bottom Folding Box with Tearable Strip Seal
templateDetails.shortDescription: Snap-lock bottom box with perforated tear strip for tamper-evident opening. Snap bottom variant of crash-bottom-carton-with-tear-strip.
templateDetails.mainUseCase: Same as crash-bottom tear strip variant but for manufacturers using snap-lock assembly tooling instead of auto-lock pre-gluing.
templateDetails.whyThisDesignExists: Same tamper-evidence need as the auto-lock tear strip variant, but using snap-lock bottom to avoid the pre-gluing step. This reduces manufacturing complexity while maintaining consumer-facing tamper evidence.

perPartRules.description: Every coordinate in every polygon, arc, or path must be a finite real number. No NaN, Infinity, or null values permitted in geometry output.
No polygon face may self-intersect. Use winding-number test before returning geometry.
Every face, crease, geometry primitive, and anchor must have a globally unique ID within the template.
Every structural crease must connect to exactly two face anchors. Crease endpoint coordinates must equal the anchor coordinates within 0.01mm tolerance.
Windows, holes, slots, perforations, and relief notches must be tagged as GeometryPrimitive. They must never be tagged as DielineCrease. Violation is a fatal schema error.
Every cutout (window, hole, slot) must lie entirely within the boundary of its target face polygon. A cutout that crosses a face boundary is invalid.
All cutouts must maintain a minimum 5mm margin from any fold crease line and a minimum 3mm margin from any cut edge.
The hinge edge of every flap (tuck flap, dust flap, lock flap) must equal the length of the anchor edge it attaches to. A tuck flap of width L must attach to a body panel edge of width L.
The face tree (parent-child fold graph) must include every face that is foldable. No face may appear twice. No foldable face may be absent from the tree.

The 'productionReady' flag on every part and template must remain false until physical prototype verification AND reference overlay comparison are complete. JSON documentation alone is insufficient for production approval.

perTemplateRules.description: The complete fold graph (all faces + creases + anchors) must pass graph validation: no orphaned faces, no broken crease connections, no circular dependencies in fold order.
Every implemented template must be able to produce a debug SVG showing all panels labeled, all creases colored, and all cutouts outlined. This is the primary visual verification tool.

Every template must be tested at minimum 3 size configurations: a very small box (50×30×20mm), a medium standard box (100×60×150mm), and a large box (300×200×400mm). All sizes must produce valid non-degenerate geometry.

Generated dieline SVG must be visually overlaid against a reference dieline image before any template is marked implementation-complete. Structural elements must align within visual inspection tolerance.
Before any template advances beyond 'spec-only' status, a reference comparison with a physical carton or verified engineering drawing must be performed.

This JSON documentation file is a reference and planning document. No template may be used for production cutting dies based solely on this documentation. Physical prototyping and expert review are mandatory.

globalConstraints.name: MaterialThicknessCompensation
globalConstraints.description: All inner-to-outer dimension conversions must use the material thickness T. Outer dimension = Inner + 2T. This applies to panel widths across fold lines in auto-lock bottoms, divider widths, insert widths, and mount widths.

globalConstraints.name: DFWMaxConstraint
globalConstraints.description: DFW (dust flap width) must always be < W/2. This is a hard constraint — violation causes physical interference between opposite dust flaps.

globalConstraints.name: GFWMinConstraint
globalConstraints.description: GFW (glue flap width) must be >= 10mm for reliable adhesive bonding.

globalConstraints.name: TFWMinConstraint
globalConstraints.description: TFW (tuck flap width) must be >= W/2 to ensure tuck flap extends past the centerline of the box opening.

globalConstraints.name: WindowMarginConstraint
globalConstraints.description: All window cutouts must maintain >= 5mm from fold creases and >= 3mm from cut edges.

globalConstraints.name: HangHoleDiameterConstraint
globalConstraints.description: Hang hole OD >= 5mm to fit standard retail peg hooks. OD <= 12mm to maintain panel integrity.

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: Exact lock notch geometry on tuck flaps
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: CefBox does not expose the lock notch dimensions as UI parameters. The exact triangular notch shape, protrusion distance, and position must be inferred from industry standard values or measured from physical sample. Standard: notch protrudes ~2–3mm from side edge, positioned at x = DFW from panel edge.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Use industry standard 2.5mm triangular notch, validate against physical reverseTuckEnd sample

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: Exact diagonal crease start/end coordinates for auto-lock bottom
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The diagonal score lines on auto-lock major flaps are the most critical geometry in the entire template library. Their exact position determines whether the bottom properly collapses flat and springs open. CefBox does not expose these as parameters — they are calculated internally.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Research standard ECMA/FEFCO auto-lock bottom construction formulas, verify with physical sample

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: 3D fold sequence and exact multi-panel layout of folded handle
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The exact arrangement of shoulder panels, bridge, and palm pad in the flat dieline, and the fold sequence to assemble the handle, cannot be fully determined from the CefBox parameter names alone. The 13 parameters suggest significant complexity.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Order physical sample from CefBox or examine reference packaging from confectionery industry

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: Gusset triangle dimensions and roof angle
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The exact dimensions of the triangular gusset fill panels and the roof angle are not parameters in the CefBox interface. They are likely calculated from L, W, and H internally. Without these, the gusset roof cannot be accurately reproduced.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Consult ECMA standard for gusset roof cartons, or obtain reference DXF from packaging supplier

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: Exact skillet end closure geometry and reversible lid hinge position
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: Skillet-end cartons have angled end walls controlled by EA1/EA2 parameters (angles in degrees). The exact geometric construction of the angled end panels and how they relate to the inner tab insert slot is not fully determinable from the parameter names alone.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Reference ECMA/GPI skillet carton standards, obtain physical cigarette-style packaging sample

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: Snap lock tongue exact shape and slot dimensions
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: CefBox does not expose tongue width, depth, or slot dimensions for snap-lock bottom as user parameters. These are calculated from L and W. Standard practice: tongue width = L/3 to L/2, depth = 5–7mm, slot = tongue + 1mm clearance.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Measure from physical snapLockBottom sample ordered from CefBox or examine ECMA Type 213

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: In the two-piece separated skillet box, it is not clear from parameters how the lid registers (aligns and stays in position) on the base when closed. There may be friction, a lip, or a secondary tab mechanism not visible in the parameter list.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Order physical sample, examine closure mechanism

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: D1-D6 fold direction sequence (valley vs mountain alternation)
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The 6 D parameters define the width of each fold segment in the accordion insert, but the fold direction (valley/mountain alternation) is not specified. Getting this wrong produces an inside-out insert.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Standard accordion fold always alternates V-M-V-M... starting with valley fold at attachment point. Verify with physical sample.

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.unknownItem: FR parameter interpretation for gusset corner fold radius
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The FR parameter on the gusset cover carton is described as 'gusset fold radius' but it is unclear whether this controls the radius of the diagonal score line transition, the curve of the corner triangle, or the folding tightness. Multiple interpretations possible.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Order physical sample and measure FR in context of assembled carton

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: Corner relief notches (small semicircular cutouts at the intersection of horizontal and vertical creases) are standard in all folding cartons but are not exposed as CefBox UI parameters. Standard industry radius is 1.5–3mm.
unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.recommendation: Implement as fixed 2mm radius semicircle at all crease intersections — verify with physical samples

unknownsAndNeedsManualReview.description: The GD parameter in carton-with-three-windows appears to control something related to the divider or windows, but its exact role among the 25 parameters in this template is ambiguous from the parameter name alone.
